text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Elevated 502 rate and DNS lookup failures for api.redwood.internal in eu-west-1. Paging oncall@sre (severity: P1).

maria: i'm on it. seeing spikes in 502s from EU LB logs + DNS NX/timeout counts up. tagging @kevin and @oscar for DNS and infra.

kevin: quick snapshot: our GeoDNS is returning two distinct A sets from different resolvers. some resolvers returning 10.0.5.99 (old, deprovisioned host) and others returning 52.34.90.10 (current ELB). TTL on record was 600s but we rotated last night. wonder if cache poisoning or stale CF edge caches.

oscar: customer impact: hosted-api error rate ~18% for EU customers over last 15m. synthetic checks triggered. ramping alert thresholds.

maria: can someone paste dig from multiple public resolvers?

kevin: paste:```
; dig @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.internal A +short
52.34.90.10
52.34.90.10
; dig @9.9.9.9 api.redwood.internal A +short
10.0.5.99
52.34.90.10
; dig @resolver-eu api.redwood.internal A +short
10.0.5.99
```

kevin: 10.0.5.99 is definitely the retired host from last week. route53 hosted zone shows only 52.34.90.10. looks like intermediate cache (Cloudflare or regional recursor) still serving older answer.

oscar: we should minimize customer impact first. propose immediate partial failover: set GeoDNS weight for eu-west to 0 and shift traffic to us-east for critical endpoints. also open CF cache purge request.

cloudops: initiating geo failover: `geodnsctl set --zone api.redwood.internal --region eu-west-1 --weight 0 --region us-east-1 --weight 100` -> returns OK (effective short).

maria: after weight change, 502 rate dropped to ~4% within 90s. still seeing occasional hits. suspect some resolvers returning 10.0.5.99, causing connection attempts to stale host -> 502.

kevin: opened CF ticket #CF-7782 asking for immediate DNS zone purge and targeted EU edge refresh. asked for confirm when complete. CF estimated 8-12m.

oscar: in parallel, i'm going to add an edge rejection for packets to 10.0.5.99 so requests fail fast rather than hang and trigger 502s. applying drop rule on managed edge.

cloudops: applied ACL to drop traffic destined for 10.0.5.99 at the edge: `acl add deny dst=10.0.5.99` -> applied.

maria: good call. if resolvers still hand out 10.0.5.99, connections will reset. that avoids hitting old host (if it still responds with broken app).

kevin: monitoring dig probes to a wide set of resolvers. quick probe log:```
17:42:01, 1.1.1.1, 52.34.90.10
17:42:03, 8.8.8.8, 52.34.90.10
17:42:05, resolver-eu1, 10.0.5.99
17:42:08, resolver-eu1, 52.34.90.10
17:42:30, resolver-eu2, 52.34.90.10
```

kevin: looks like most recursors switched after the purge kick, some lagged by <1m.

oscar: status update draft for status.redwood.com: "Investigating partial routing inconsistency in EU causing increased API 502 responses. Mitigation in progress (traffic rerouted; DNS cache purge requested)." @status-team will you post?

status-team: posting now.

maria: let's double-check there are no static references to 10.0.5.99 in any load balancer or service config. I scanned infra inventory but will also grep our config repo.

kevin: found a holdover entry in an old haproxy map on eu1-lb-old (not in active pool) referencing 10.0.5.99 for legacy backend health checks. removed and reloaded haproxy config.

maria: that explains residual hits. thanks.

cloudops: can we confirm Cloudflare has completed purge?

kevin: CF updated: purge completed at 17:50, edge confirmations returned for EU POPs.

maria: monitoring: 502s back to baseline, synthetic checks green. moving to MONITORING. keeping CF ticket open for 24h verification.

oscar: follow-ups to track: 1) lower TTL before decommission step (pre-rotate at 60s for 24h), 2) add checklist item to blank old IPs from any config maps and LB maps, 3) automate CF zone purge as part of DNS record change playbook.

incident-bot: Incident transitioned to MONITORING. Lead: maria. Severity reduced P1 -> P2.

maria: thanks all. i'll own the postmortem and RFC for the DNS decommission checklist. tagging @kevin to own CF follow-up.

oscar: will open INC-3892 and attach probe logs and HAProxy diff.

maria: handing off to daytime oncall in 15m. leaving channel open for any late regressions.

kevin: attaching dig logs to INC-3892. closing live thread.
